planting.note: Plant fresh seed in fall or container-grown trees in spring in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun; monkey puzzle is dioecious, so both a male and a female tree are needed for nut production, and trees need 30-40 years to reach seed-bearing maturity.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in full sun with plenty of room, since this striking Chilean and Argentine conifer eventually becomes a very large, unmistakable tree with thick, reptilian, spirally arranged branches covered in sharp, overlapping, scale-like leaves — an architectural specimen unlike anything else commonly grown. Native to the cool temperate rainforests and volcanic slopes of the southern Andes, it is the sacred tree of the Indigenous Mapuche and Pehuenche peoples, whose name for the tree, pehuen, gave the Pehuenche people their name as "people of the pehuen," reflecting the tree's central place in their diet and culture for millennia. Female cones take about three years to mature and release large, edible, chestnut-like seeds (piñones) that are traditionally roasted, boiled, or ground into flour, but a tree needs both a male and female cone-bearing tree nearby and several decades of growth before it produces a nut crop, making it a multigenerational planting rather than a quick food source. It tolerates cold well but resents the sustained summer heat and humidity of the Gulf South, performing best in cool-summer, mild-winter climates such as the Pacific Northwest or higher elevations.
sources: Chile Forestal / CONAF — Araucaria araucana Conservation Notes
